evidence.estrutura: Crenshaw analyzes structural power across legal institutions but does not advocate a specific federal-versus-unitary architecture; modest decentralist/institutional reform tendency.
evidence.representacao: Civil-rights and intersectionality scholarship argues for recognition and inclusion of people marginalized by law and institutions; strongly democratic/inclusion-oriented.
evidence.poder: Her work on discrimination, policing-related harms and legal inequality favors rights constraints on coercive institutions.
evidence.imigracao: Intersectional and anti-discrimination frameworks support pluralism across race, gender and identity; relatively multicultural.
evidence.diplomacia: Foreign policy is not her principal field; human-rights orientation favors diplomacy but should remain moderate.
evidence.intervencao: No detailed military-intervention doctrine; anti-domination principles support restraint.
evidence.economia: Structural inequality analysis supports redistributive and anti-discrimination interventions, though she is not an ownership-system theorist.
evidence.controle: Legal remedies and institutional regulation support moderate public control, not command planning.
evidence.comercio: No substantive trade doctrine is established.
evidence.religiao: Her public scholarship is secular legal analysis rather than religious governance.
evidence.moral: Intersectionality, feminist legal theory and civil-rights scholarship place her strongly on progressive equality.
evidence.tecnologia: Technology is not central to her core theory; moderate modernist.
